title: forensic-telemetry-snapshotting-and-slo-evidence-retention-policy-2023
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview
========

Purpose: Define a reproducible, cost-aware process for capturing forensic telemetry snapshots that provide SLO-related evidence for incident review, post-incident analysis, and regulatory audit. This policy aligns retention windows for metrics, traces, logs, and request-level artifacts with incident severity, SLO class, and cost budget.

Scope: Applies to all services that carry an explicit SLO in the model-serving and routing stack (platform services, model inference, request-queueing, caching layers). This does not replace long-term archival for compliance; it prescribes a short-to-medium-term snapshot strategy that supports fast forensics and hypothesis-driven RCA.

Background and motivation
-------------------------
- SRE investigations require coherent cross-signal evidence (metrics + traces + logs + token-level samples) covering pre-incident, incident, and recovery windows.
- Keeping high-fidelity telemetry for all services indefinitely is cost-prohibitive; careless retention causes escalated cloud billing and slows tooling.
- A snapshot-first approach captures high-value data around SLO-impacting events while keeping the default retention conservative.

Key concepts
------------
- Snapshot: A logically consistent bundle of telemetry for a service over a time-window (start_ts, end_ts) stored as a named artifact (e.g., snapshot: inference-service/us-west-2/2023-09-15T14:04Z).
- Evidence tier: Classification of snapshot fidelity and retention based on severity and SLO tier. Evidence tiers: minimal, standard, full, archival-request.
- SLO class: Each service is mapped to an SLO class (gold, silver, bronze) that defines acceptable latency/availability thresholds and default evidence tier.

Evidence tiers and retention (table)
-----------------------------------
| Evidence tier  | Contents included                                                            | Retention (from capture) |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| minimal        | aggregated metrics (1s resolution for critical metrics), sparse traces (sampled 0.1%), error counts | 7 days                  |
| standard       | metrics (1s), full traces for top N error traces (N=500), request logs (indexed), sampling of token outputs (1%) | 30 days                 |
| full           | metrics (1s), all traces for affected trace IDs, raw request bodies (redacted), token-level output archives (per-tenant), debug profile dumps, heap/malloc snapshots if requested | 90 days                 |
| archival-request | Anything in full tier plus export to cold archive (GCS/Azure blob w/ 7-year retention) | per compliance request  |

Service SLO class mapping (example table)
-----------------------------------------
| Service pattern                | Default SLO class | Default evidence tier |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------- | --------------------- |
| public hosted text-generation  | gold              | full                  |
| internal routing/orchestration | silver            | standard              |
| low-traffic experimental model | bronze            | minimal               |

Trigger conditions for snapshot capture
---------------------------------------
1. Automatic triggers (system):
   - SLO burn-rate > 3x sustained for 10 minutes for a gold service.
   - Error-rate spike crossing configured SLI thresholds (5xx, model-inference-errors) exceeding 3σ relative to baseline.
   - Tail-latency (p99.9) exceeds threshold by >2x for >5 minutes.
2. Manual triggers (oncall):
   - Pager duty escalation for incidents where SLOs are impacted (any severity).
   - Postmortem author requests extended snapshot for targeted investigation.
3. Scheduled triggers:
   - Canary rollouts: capture 60 minutes before and 60 minutes after canary start for any rollout touching production models.

Snapshot composition and schema
-------------------------------
Each snapshot artifact must include a small manifest (manifest.json) with the following fields (stored as top-level keys in the bundle):
- snapshot_id, service_name, cluster, region, start_ts, end_ts, trigger_reason, evidence_tier, initiated_by, size_bytes, object_list (array of file names).

Storage locations and naming conventions
---------------------------------------
- Primary ephemeral store: object://sre-telemetry-snapshots/{region}/{service}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/{snapshot_id}.tar.gz
- Long-term export (archival-request): gs://sre-archive/evidence/{service}/{snapshot_id}/ (cold storage)
- Naming: {service}/{region}/{YYYYMMDD}T{HHMMSS}-{trigger}-{tier}

Cost control and quotas
-----------------------
- Each team has a monthly snapshot budget measured in GB. Default: 100 GB/month for teams owning silver/gold services; experimental teams start at 10 GB/month.
- Snapshot capture that would exceed the monthly quota must be reviewed by SRE lead and product owner; automated throttling will switch the evidence tier down one level during quota exhaustion.
- Compression: snapshots should use zstd -19 by default; token archives may be compressed with delta encoding for size reduction.

Operational runbook: capturing a snapshot (automated path)
---------------------------------------------------------
1. Detection: Monitoring system raises an 'slo-burn' alarm and posts a notification to #sre-alerts with alarm metadata.
2. Snapshot manager service (sre-snapshotter) reads the alarm, computes the affected time-window (T0-5m to now +5m), and schedules snapshot jobs across instrumentation backends.
3. Backends collect: metrics export (OpenMetrics), traces (Jaeger/OTLP), logs (indexed request logs), request bodies (if configured and redaction policies permit), and sampling of token outputs for inference requests.
4. Snapshot bundling: collected files are validated (manifest checksum), compressed, and uploaded to the ephemeral store. A notification containing snapshot_id and location is emitted to the incident channel and attached to the alert.

Manual capture (oncall)
-----------------------
1. Oncall run: /usr/local/bin/sre-snapshot-cli create --service inference-service --window "-10m:+10m" --tier full --reason "oncall_manual_capture"
2. CLI prompts for justification (free text) and optional add-on flags: --include-heap-dump, --include-token-archive.
3. Snapshot uploaded; CLI prints snapshot_id and short-link, and adds an entry to the incident evidence index.

Evidence handoff and post-incident process
------------------------------------------
1. During incident: attach snapshot link to the incident timeline. Oncall must add short justification and the list of hypothesis owners.
2. Post-incident: the incident reviewer will select snapshots for inclusion in the postmortem package. Evidence that remains required for regulatory reasons is forwarded to archival-request and exported to cold storage.
3. Evidence deletion: unless moved to archival, snapshots older than their retention period are auto-deleted by the snapshot manager. Deletions are logged and reversible only via a formal SRE change request within 30 days.

Access and redaction rules
-------------------------
- Principle of least privilege: access to snapshot artifacts requires an Evidence ACL. Default access: SRE oncall and service owners. Additional access granted via ticket and documented justification.
- PII and customer data: snapshots must run automatic redaction pipelines for request bodies and token outputs. Redaction rules are maintained in /infra/configs/snapshot-redaction.yaml.
- Token-level outputs: default sampling rate 1% unless evidence tier is full where sampling is 100% for affected keys/trace IDs. Token archives are stored encrypted with KMS keys scoped to the owning team.

Verification and quality gates
-----------------------------
- Every automated snapshot must pass a manifest checksum and schema validation before being considered evidence-grade.
- Nightly job validates that snapshots referenced by open incidents exist and are accessible; missing artifacts raise an operational ticket.

Runbook: retrieving a snapshot for analysis
------------------------------------------
1. Use the snapshot browser: https://console.internal/sre/snapshots and filter by service/incident id/date.
2. For CLI access: sre-snapshot-cli fetch --id {snapshot_id} --output /tmp/{snapshot_id}.tar.gz
3. Local inspection: tar -I "zstd -d" -xvf /tmp/{snapshot_id}.tar.gz && less {snapshot_root}/manifest.json
4. Common queries:
   - top error traces: jq '.traces | sort_by(.error_count) | reverse | .[:50]' manifest.json
   - metric deltas: prometheus diff queries with provided metrics CSV

Governance and review cadence
----------------------------
- SRE cadence: Monthly snapshot usage review with finance to adjust budgets and quotas.
- Audits: Quarterly evidence-sampling audit to ensure redaction rules are effective and access logs are complete.
- Postmortem requirements: Any Sev 2+ incident that used a snapshot must document the snapshot_id list and retention decisions in the postmortem.

Implementation notes for engineering
----------------------------------
- The snapshot manager will expose a REST endpoint: POST /v1/snapshots with JSON payload (flat fields only): {service, start_ts, end_ts, tier, initiated_by, reason}. Responses include snapshot_id and presigned upload locations for collectors.
- Collectors must stream data to presigned locations and mark completion via POST /v1/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/complete.
- Use protobuf for manifest serialization for performance; provide a human-readable manifest.json alongside a manifest.pb for tooling.

Logging and observability for snapshot pipeline
--------------------------------------------
- Instrumentation: success_rate, median_capture_time, size_bytes_histogram, failed_uploads.
- SLO for snapshot pipeline: 95% of automated snapshot captures complete and are available within 6 minutes of trigger; 99% within 15 minutes.

Appendix: example CLI snippets
-----------------------------
- Create automated capture (example):
  sre-snapshot-cli create --service routing-proxy --tier standard --window "-5m:+10m" --reason "slo_burn_detected"

- Fetch and inspect manifest:
  sre-snapshot-cli fetch --id snapshot-20231102-az1-12345 --output /tmp/snapshot.tar.gz
  tar -I "zstd -d" -xvf /tmp/snapshot.tar.gz
  jq . /tmp/snapshot/manifest.json

Change log
----------
- 2023-09-15: Initial draft and roll-out to SRE teams.
- 2024-03-12: Added quota throttling rules and compression defaults.
- 2024-11-02: Formalized evidence ACL and archival-request workflow; updated retention windows.
